contact.headline: Get in touch

contact.data_heading: Who is responsible for your data
contact.data_body: Sebastian Rosiński and Dawid Adamczyk are joint controllers of the data processed in the Kidalu apps, with an equal share in the project. You can send a request for access, correction or deletion to either address above — whichever of us reads it first will answer. Data breach reports we handle together.

czytanie.name: Reading by Syllables
czytanie.tagline: Your child reads on their own, one syllable at a time.

features.title: Coloured syllables
features.body: Text is split automatically by Polish syllable rules and neighbouring syllables get different colours. The child sees where one ends and the next begins.

features.title: A library of texts
features.body: Fairy tales, poems and stories ready to read, including classics of Polish children's literature from Wolne Lektury.

features.title: Your own text
features.body: Type anything: a postcard from grandma, a shopping list, a favourite song — and see it in coloured syllables.

features.title: Tuned to your child
features.body: Set syllable colours, font size and background theme to whatever your child reads most comfortably.

features.title: Print and PDF
features.body: Export any text and print it to practise away from the screen.

features.title: Reading progress
features.body: The app remembers what your child has read and shows how far they got in each text.

czytanie.lead: The app splits every text into syllables and colours them alternately. Your child's eye stops getting lost mid-word, and reading turns from guessing into assembling.

who.text: Children aged 4–8 who are learning to read

privacy: No ads or promotional content aimed at children
We build no behavioural profiles and never link data between apps
A parent creates the account and can delete it permanently, with all its data, at any time

literki.name: Letters and Numbers
literki.tagline: Writing letters and numbers with a finger on the screen.

features.title: Tracing, not drawing
features.body: The child follows the model rather than drawing freely — the app checks whether the hand stays on the line.

features.title: Fixed stroke order
features.body: Every character has a defined stroke order and direction, matching the school handwriting of the chosen country. The app never contradicts the exercise book.

features.title: Poland, Germany, Austria
features.body: For Poland, 35 upper and 35 lower case letters including ą, ć, ę, ł, ń, ó, ś, ź, ż. For Germany and Austria, the alphabet with ä, ö, ü, ß. Digits 0 to 9 everywhere.

features.title: Handwriting style and difficulty
features.body: Six school scripts to choose from in Germany, two each in Poland and Austria. The tolerated deviation from the trace is set in the parent panel.

features.title: No time pressure
features.body: No timer, no attempt limit. Accuracy counts, not speed.

features.title: Works offline
features.body: All you need is a touchscreen. No account, no sign-in.

literki.lead: The child traces the shape while the app watches the order and direction of every stroke. You pick the country at the start — it sets the alphabet, the handwriting style and the animals to collect.
